title: Sketch map of the Arctic regions at the time of Franklin's last expedition, and the drift of the Fox down Baffin's Bay
creator: Francis Leopold McClintock
description: Two maps on one leaf at the front of McClintock's narrative: what was known of the Arctic when Franklin sailed in 1845, and the track of the Fox as she was carried 1,194 miles south down Baffin Bay in the pack through the winter of 1857-58 before she could begin her search at all.

title: Frontispiece: the Fox in the ice
creator: after Captain May
description: The frontispiece plate of the Fox among the floes, from a drawing by Captain May of the Royal Navy, who supplied most of the book's illustrations.

title: Moonlight in the Arctic regions
creator: Captain May
description: The winter moon over the pack during the Fox's involuntary drift down Baffin Bay, 1857-58.

title: Taking an observation on the floe
creator: Captain May
description: Officers at an instrument on the ice during the drift, with the ship in the background.

title: The Greenlander's supper appropriated by a bear
creator: Captain May
description: A polar bear helping itself to a Greenlander's meal - one of the comic plates May drew for the narrative.

title: Esquimaux imitating animals to induce Europeans to approach
creator: Captain Allen Young
description: Inuit hunters mimicking game to draw the ship's people towards them. McClintock's book turns on Inuit testimony, and this plate is a rare picture of the approach that produced it.

title: Sledges under the coastal cliffs
creator: Captain May
description: A sledge party working along the foot of a high coast.

title: The Fox arriving at Beechey Island
creator: Captain May
description: The Fox coming in to Beechey Island, where Franklin's people had wintered in 1845-46 and where McClintock landed the marble tablet Lady Franklin sent north.

title: M'Clintock in his boat sailing through Bellot Strait
creator: Captain May
description: McClintock under sail in the boat through Bellot Strait, the narrow tide-swept channel between Somerset Island and the Boothia Peninsula, the northernmost point of the American mainland.

title: Dog sledge and scout party
creator: Captain May
description: A dog team and scouting party on the march - the method, learned from Inuit and from Carl Petersen's Greenland experience, that let McClintock cover the ground earlier searches could not.

title: Interior of the observatory
creator: Captain May
description: Inside the magnetic and astronomical observatory built ashore at Port Kennedy for the winter of 1858-59.

title: Walruses: a family party
creator: Captain Allen Young
description: A group of walrus on the ice, drawn from Allen Young's sketch.

title: The search parties on the march
creator: Captain May
description: A sledge party crossing broken ice on the spring journeys of 1859 that found the Victory Point record, the boat and the skeletons on King William Island.

title: Isolated iceberg
creator: P. Skelton, after Captain Allen Young
description: A single berg standing in open water, engraved by Skelton from Allen Young's sketch.

title: Sketch map of the Arctic Archipelago
creator: Francis Leopold McClintock
description: The large folding map at the end of the narrative, laying out the archipelago as it stood after the Fox's voyage, with the search tracks and the ground covered on King William Island where Franklin's people died.
